idea-plugin.name: Pixel Office - AI Agent Visualizer
idea-plugin.description:
Pixel Agents for IntelliJ

Turn your Claude Code terminal sessions into animated pixel art characters in a virtual office. Each terminal you open spawns a character that walks around, sits at desks, and visually reflects what the agent is doing in real time.

Features

  • One agent, one character — every Claude Code terminal gets its own animated character
  • Live activity tracking — characters animate based on what the agent is doing (writing, reading, running commands)
  • Sub-agent visualization — Task/Agent sub-agents spawn as separate characters, including async background agents
  • Office layout editor — design your office with floors, walls, and 80+ furniture items
  • Multiple themes — default office, alien, cat, and zoo themes with unique characters and furniture
  • Speech bubbles — visual indicators when an agent is waiting or needs permission
  • Sound notifications — optional chime when an agent finishes its turn
  • Persistent layouts — office design saved across IDE restarts
  • Animated furniture — wall clocks tick, desk fans spin, water coolers bubble

How It Works

Pixel Agents watches Claude Code's JSONL transcript files to track what each agent is doing. No modifications to Claude Code are needed — it's purely observational. The webview runs a lightweight game loop with canvas rendering, BFS pathfinding, and a character state machine.

Getting Started

  1. Install Claude Code CLI
  2. Open the Pixel Agents tool window (bottom panel)
  3. Click + Agent to spawn a Claude Code terminal
  4. Watch the character react as Claude works on your code

Based on Pixel Agents for VS Code by Pablo De Lucca. Ported to the IntelliJ Platform with additional features.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.5

Compatibility

  • Removed the until-build upper bound — the plugin now stays available on new IDE releases (2026.2 / build 262 and later) instead of being delisted

New Claude models

  • Model chips for the Claude 5 family: FABLE 5, MYTH 5, SON 5, OPUS 4.8 (previously fell back to a grey unknown chip)
  • Context-window scale corrected to 1M for Fable 5 / Mythos 5 / Sonnet 5 / Sonnet 4.6, so the HP gauge and HUD percentage are accurate
  • Updated cost table (Opus $5/$25, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5, Fable & Mythos $10/$50)

Behavior fixes

  • Background Bash tasks keep their character active after the turn ends, instead of going idle while the command still runs
  • Sub-agent watchers now time out at 30s (they were reusing the 60s main-agent threshold)
  • 5-hour token usage chip in the HUD now actually populates on IntelliJ (the backend never sent the data before)

Unified view

  • New Unified View (Show Other Sources) setting, off by default. When enabled, agents from other IDE windows and CLI sessions appear at 85% transparency alongside your own

UI polish

  • Replaced glyphs the pixel font could not render (which fell back to OS emoji), unified the close button across panels, and pixelated the native sliders/checkboxes in the layout editor

1.0.4

  • Git worktree support — Claude sessions running in a worktree of the open repository now show up in the same office. Worktrees created while the IDE is running are picked up within 5s, no restart needed
  • Agents adopted from a worktree carry a ↳branch suffix on their label, persisted across IDE restarts

1.0.3

UX

  • Status bubble stays above every working agent (toned-down ambient style; full styling on hover/select)
  • Context window HP gauge next to each agent's label — muted forest-green / gold / brick-red bar shows 200K context usage; % number appears on hover/select
  • Model indicator chip in the activity bubble (OPUS / SON / HAI) — pixel-art styling with muted palette + 1px outline + hard offset shadow. Reads message.model from each assistant record
  • Session totals on hover/select — cumulative tokens + estimated USD cost line below the bubble (e.g. 12.4K tok • $0.18 est). Cost is approximate, based on the last observed model's published rates with cache_create at 1.25x input and cache_read at 0.10x
  • Keyboard zoom shortcuts — + / - step zoom; Ctrl/Cmd+0 resets to auto-fit default. Ignored while typing in inputs
  • Unified all agent stale-removal thresholds to 60 seconds (previously 30 / 60 / 120)

Stability — agent lifecycle

  • Fixed main agent not disappearing after 60s when Claude was Ctrl+C'd mid-permission-prompt (permissionSent stuck flag bypassed dead-session check)
  • Fixed race where clicking + Agent could spawn duplicate characters (knownJsonlFiles registered before claude launch)
  • Fixed sub-agent characters disappearing on webview reload while Task was still running (taskStatus preserved on AsyncSubagent)
  • Fixed /clear leaving pendingSubagentIds / hadToolsInTurn stuck, causing mis-bound sub-agents and missing waiting indicators
  • Fixed stale agentSeats entries leaking across IDE restarts and causing seat/palette drift on new agents
  • Reconciliation: existingAgents message now removes ghost characters/state the webview has but the extension does not
  • TOCTOU guard: dead-session check re-verifies jsonlFile path before removing an agent that may have just been reassigned via /clear
  • Fixed startJsonlPoll using a captured stale agent reference; now re-fetches live state every tick

Stability — webview

  • Guarded addSubagent capacity sentinel (returns 0) so phantom sub-agent records are not pushed when the visible-character cap is reached
  • Sub-agent characters now stop their typing/reading animation when their last tool finishes
  • subagentClear now also removes the corresponding React record so labels don't outlive the OfficeState character

Resource leaks

  • Made onWebviewReady infrastructure init idempotent — JCEF panel toggles no longer accumulate duplicate TerminalDetector / sessionAliveCheck / periodicDiscovery timers
  • stopWatching now also clears subagentStartTimes / subagentLastActivity bookkeeping (prevents long-session memory growth)

API & build

  • Replaced scheduled-for-removal TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget with createShellWidget for forward compatibility with future IntelliJ releases
  • Cleared Kotlin compiler warnings (shadowed name, unused parameter)
  • Migrated extension println calls (35 sites) and webview console.log calls (14 sites) to proper Logger.debug / debug() gates — silent in production
  • Marked shared assetsDir as @Volatile to harden visibility between setTheme and asset loading threads
  • Added unit-test infrastructure: JUnit 5 (Kotlin) + vitest (webview), 60 tests covering pure helpers; CI workflow runs both on push/PR with plugin verifier on main

1.0.0

  • Initial release — IntelliJ Platform port of Pixel Agents
  • JCEF-based webview with full canvas rendering
  • Claude Code JSONL transcript watching with hybrid polling
  • Async sub-agent file tracking (separate JSONL files)
  • Multiple themes: default, alien, cat, zoo
  • Layout editor with undo/redo, floor/wall painting, furniture placement
  • Auto-animated furniture (clocks, fans, water coolers)
  • Agent persistence across IDE restarts
  • External session adoption (terminals started without --session-id)
  • Dead session detection and cleanup
